second_order: Choosing Catholic pictures and where to put them
theme_note: Participants turn an open invitation into candidate subjects, templates, coordinates, scale, and an order for adding details. What varies is the picture—Sacred Hearts, crosses, keys, coats of arms, or flags—and whether the contribution is a question, proposal, template, or design constraint.
regrouped_from: split during the full grouping review from an initial making-Catholic-pictures group because choosing a design and location is different from placing and holding it

second_order: Playing April Fools on one another
theme_note: Members stage false papal news or religious jokes and then spot, explain, enjoy, resist, or redirect them. The variation lies in whether a turn springs the joke, admits being fooled, corrects its premise, objects to the joke, or carries the exchange into birthday talk.
regrouped_from: reviewed after all slices; retained as one practice because the codes are turns in making and responding to the room's own April Fools jokes, not canvas work

second_order: Following and disputing the crusader shield plan
theme_note: Participants call for a crusader-themed design, defend or alter it, argue over who began it and who was invited, and correct which orders the shields represent. The variation is between practical design work and disputes about ownership and Catholic relevance, but all turns work out whose shield plan should govern.
regrouped_from: reviewed after later flag and Sacred Heart slices; kept distinct because these codes resolve one shared crusader-shield plan and its ownership dispute rather than Catholic pixel work generally

second_order: Applying subreddit rules to r/place posts
theme_note: Room-operated moderation applies link and relevance rules to event posts. What varies is the rule invoked—using an np link or belonging in the subreddit—and whether enforcement is automatic or human.
regrouped_from: reviewed after all slices; retained separately because rule enforcement is a community practice toward event talk, not a step in making the canvas designs

second_order: Placing, repairing, and defending Catholic marks
theme_note: Participants commit pixels, recruit hands, restore erased work, scale designs to what can be held, and report whether marks survived. The variation is among crosses, flags, shields, and Sacred Hearts, and among starting, defending, losing, and partially completing them.
regrouped_from: split during the slice-07 grouping review from choosing Catholic pictures because these codes report doing and holding the pixel work rather than deciding what it should be

second_order: Finding room among defended logos and neighbours
theme_note: Participants work around existing claims by relocating, answering warnings, asking neighbours for space or permission, and recognising who governs or defends an area. What varies is the neighbour—sports fans, checkerboards, green lattice, Italy, France—and whether the response is avoidance, negotiation, or continued pressure.
regrouped_from: split from an initial building-and-defending group because these codes concern accommodating other groups' existing claims rather than placing Catholic pixels

second_order: Moving pixel plans into dedicated places
theme_note: When the room is too small or confused, participants point helpers toward another subreddit or propose a dedicated channel and eventually name a headquarters. The variation is between an inherited r/CKcrusaders plan, unsuccessful requests to an ally, proposed IRC or Discord, and the demonstrated move to r/vcplace.
regrouped_from: split from finding room during the full review because changing the organising venue is different from negotiating canvas space

theme_note: A member asks for help removing a pornographic drawing, another joins, and the requester reports it more or less destroyed. The turns vary only by call, uptake, and qualified outcome, so this small practice remains its own theme.
regrouped_from: reviewed after all slices; retained as a small standalone theme because removing rejected content does not belong with making or defending Catholic imagery

second_order: Continuing the Vatican flag on a mirror
theme_note: After the original canvas closes, participants rebuild the Vatican flag on Pxls.space, work around its timer, report the flag complete, and begin lettering and blueprint revisions. The variation is between rallying, showing progress, solving placement friction, claiming completion, and opening the unfinished Deogratias/r/catholicism extension.
regrouped_from: reviewed against the original-canvas flag codes and retained separately because participants explicitly continue on a replacement canvas after r/place has closed
